definition: Life space is a person-level aspect of functioning that can become constricted over time. In this source, life space constriction is considered as a possible pathway linking physical and cognitive decline with later dementia risk.

reasons: The packet only supports that life space constriction was evaluated as a possible mediator between physical/cognitive decline and incident dementia risk; it does not support defining life space itself as a person-level aspect of functioning.
The claim that life space can become constricted over time is not stated in the packet as a definition of the term, only as part of the study’s research focus on life space constriction.
The definition adds an explanatory pathway claim in a way that goes beyond the source’s wording and should not be presented as a settled definition.

The packet text does not define “life space” as a “person-level aspect of functioning,” nor does it state that it “can become constricted over time.” The only provided support is that the study evaluates “life space constriction” as a mediator.

While the packet does support that life space constriction has a mediating role in the pathway between physio-cognitive aging trajectories (physical and cognitive decline) and “incident dementia risk,” the definition’s additional wording about life space being a specific person-level functioning aspect is not supported by the supplied excerpt.
Because the definition includes unsupported substantive claims beyond what is evidenced in the provided packet excerpt, the overall definition is not defensible.
